action_summary: Before building last round's named bottleneck I measured whether it binds: 73% of /usr/bin is unreadable, so it does. Then the measurement destroyed round 11's result. Running every judge against every OTHER REAL KIND, not against a nonsense decoy, shows gzip -t exits 0 on a real ZIP (gzip 1.12 prints OK), tar -tf exits 0 on a gzip, python ast accepts a JSON document ({"a":1} IS a valid python expression), and utf8_text accepts json/tar/python. All four passed round 11's test, so round 11's claim of seven judges was wrong: a scan built on them would have reported a zip file as gzip -- the lying-name failure arriving through the validator. A candidate must now reject every other real kind, and the refusals name which kinds they accepted. gzip and tar were recovered by ASKING A DIFFERENT QUESTION of the same program. A second correction followed: the strict test is right for a kind and wrong for a NESTED kind, because a .py file IS utf8 text; with it alone, 0% of /usr/share/doc was readable. Two admission classes now, EXCLUSIVE and NESTED. Coverage on a real machine: 393/400 = 98.2%, with /usr/bin going from 73% unreadable to 80/80 after earning an ELF judge.

agent_orientation.earlier_routes_exhausted_reason: Three routes rejected. (1) Keep seven judges and note the caveat: a validator that answers a different question is worse than a missing one, because it silently mislabels. (2) Refuse nested kinds entirely: measured, it kept 5 judges and made 0% of /usr/share/doc readable -- the cure was worse than the disease. (3) Add a second decoy: a decoy is still not a real kind, so it repeats the same structural blindness one step later.
